h1: Modesto ADU Rules & Land Use Law: Size, Setbacks, Parking & Permits
long_content:
Which law applies to a Modesto ADU: city, county or state?

All three, in this order. Modesto's own code governs first: the city is incorporated, so the rules that count inside the city limits are Title 10, Chapter 4, Article 5 of the Modesto Municipal Code (sections 10-4.501 to 10-4.512), not Stanislaus County's Chapter 21.74. Where a local standard conflicts with California Government Code section 66310 et seq., state law applies — section 10-4.512 says so directly.

One practical consequence: the county publishes free ADU plan sets (405 sq ft, 744 sq ft and 1,192 sq ft, drawn to the 2025 California Building Code) that can be used in Modesto as well as in the unincorporated county. For a new-construction detached ADU, those drawings can remove most of the design cost before you ever speak to a plan reviewer.

How many ADUs can I build in Modesto?

  • Single-family lot: up to two additional units — any combination of attached, detached or converted ADU, plus one JADU.
  • Multifamily building: ADUs inside existing non-livable space can be at least one and up to 25% of the existing units; up to 8 detached ADUs on a lot with an existing multifamily building, and up to 2 detached ADUs where the multifamily building is proposed.
  • Places of worship: up to two detached ADUs of no more than 1,200 sq ft each, with 4 ft interior side and rear setbacks and no extra parking where one existing space is reserved per ADU.

California also requires Modesto to approve certain ADU types ministerially, and the city's code says so explicitly in section 10-4.511. Those units cannot be refused because the property has non-conforming zoning conditions, and correcting those conditions cannot be made a condition of approval.

Modesto ADU size, height and setback limits

Detached ADU maximum1,200 sq ft, and never more than the main home's floor area
Attached ADU maximum50% of the main home's floor area, but the city cannot refuse an attached ADU of up to 800 sq ft
JADU maximum500 sq ft, inside the walls of the house
Minimum ADU sizeNone in the code — state law bars a minimum that would exclude an efficiency unit

Parking in Modesto: one space maximum, none in six cases

Modesto cannot require more than one off-street space for an ADU, and a tandem space in an existing driveway counts. Uncovered spaces may sit in the required front setback where a driveway already exists, or in the rear setback where the lot has alley access. No space at all may be required in these six situations:

  • the ADU is within 1/2 mile walking distance of public transit;
  • it is in an architecturally or historically significant district;
  • it is part of the main residence or an existing accessory structure;
  • the street requires permits but no permit is offered to the ADU occupant;
  • a car-share vehicle is available within one block;
  • the ADU permit is filed together with a new single-family or multifamily dwelling permit on the same lot.

Parking that disappears when a garage or carport is demolished or converted does not have to be replaced.

Modesto's ADU Express program: same-day plan review

Modesto runs an appointment-based ADU Express service that coordinates Building Safety, Fire, Planning and Engineering in one review session for ADU and JADU projects that qualify for ministerial approval. Same-day approval requires plans prepared by a professional designer, licensed architect or engineer. Appointments are booked through Building Safety at 209-577-5232, extension 0; the program's flyer lists Tuesday sessions from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m.

The city describes an eight-step path: create a plan, get planning advice, prepare the submittal package, apply through the eTRAKiT portal, hire licensed professionals, go through staff plan review, receive the permit, then build and inspect. Housing questions go to the Community Development Division at housing@modestogov.com or 209-577-5211; planning questions to 209-577-5267.

What a Modesto ADU costs: $2,429 per permit

The FY 2026-27 Building Safety fee schedule charges $2,429 per permit for accessory dwelling units and small dwellings up to 1,200 sq ft, covering mechanical, plumbing and electrical work, payable at application. On top of that, no impact fee applies to an ADU under 750 sq ft, and above that threshold fees must be charged in proportion to the main dwelling's square footage — not at the full rate for a new house.

Financial help exists: CalHFA's ADU grant programme has offered up to $40,000, and local options include the Valley First Credit Union Expand.Enhance.Empower loan programme and Stanislaus Equity Partners. Beware of older guides quoting Modesto's "ADU Development Fees 2022-2023" document — that link is dead and the numbers are obsolete.

Conversions, as-built drawings and unpermitted space

If you are converting a garage, a workshop or an unpermitted living area, Modesto does not require a setback beyond what fire and safety need, allows expansion of up to 150 sq ft of the existing structure for ingress and egress, waives lot coverage limits for units of 800 sq ft or less, and prohibits the city from requiring you to correct non-conforming zoning conditions as a condition of approval.

What reviewers will still need is a clear picture of how the structure actually exists today — that is what a conversion set of drawings has to document. California law also prevents the city from denying a permit because of building-code violations or unpermitted structures, as long as the ADU itself is built to code.

faqs.q: What does Modesto land use law say about ADUs?
faqs.a: ADUs are governed by the Modesto Municipal Code Title 10, Chapter 4, Article 5, sections 10-4.501 to 10-4.512. That article sets where ADUs are allowed, the size and height limits, setbacks, parking, the JADU owner-occupancy deed restriction and the fee rules, and it says that where a local standard conflicts with California Government Code section 66310 et seq., state law applies. It is a city code, not a county one: Stanislaus County's Chapter 21.74 has no force inside Modesto's city limits.

faqs.q: Does Modesto require a minimum ADU size?
faqs.a: No. Modesto's code sets no minimum floor area for an ADU, and California law forbids a minimum that would prevent an efficiency unit. Guides quoting a 150 sq ft minimum for Modesto are not supported by the current code.

faqs.q: How much does a Modesto ADU permit cost?
faqs.a: $2,429 per permit for an ADU or small dwelling up to 1,200 sq ft under the FY 2026-27 fee schedule, including mechanical, plumbing and electrical, payable when you apply. Separately, no impact fee applies to an ADU under 750 sq ft, and larger units are charged proportionally to the main home rather than at full new-house rates.

faqs.q: Can I convert my garage into an ADU in Modesto?
faqs.a: Yes. A conversion inside or replacing an existing structure needs only enough setback for fire and safety, may expand the structure by up to 150 sq ft for ingress and egress, is exempt from lot coverage limits up to 800 sq ft, and the lost parking does not have to be replaced.

faqs.q: Do I have to live in the property to rent out a Modesto ADU?
faqs.a: No for an ADU — Modesto does not require owner occupancy for ADUs, and state law bars the requirement. A JADU is different: before final inspection the owner must record a deed restriction agreeing to live in the JADU or the rest of the house at all times, unless the owner is a government agency, land trust or housing organisation. Rentals must run 30 days or longer.

faqs.q: How long does a Modesto ADU permit take?
faqs.a: Ministerial review must be completed within 60 days of a complete application, and if the city takes no action the ADU is deemed approved. Modesto also runs ADU Express, an appointment-based session that reviews an eligible ADU with Building Safety, Fire, Planning and Engineering at once and can approve it the same day when the plans are prepared by a licensed professional.

long_content:
Vallejo's ADU ordinance changed in 2026 — what that means for you

Vallejo repealed and replaced Chapter 16.303 in its entirety. Ordinance No. 1890 N.C.(2d) was introduced on 4 August 2026, adopted on 8 September 2026, and became effective on 8 October 2026 after the standard 30-day period. Until that date the old six-section chapter still governs.

There is a second layer to the story. On 8 October 2025 the state Department of Housing and Community Development wrote to Vallejo noting that the most recent ADU ordinance on file dated from 2018 and may not comply with state ADU law. Under Government Code section 66316, an ADU ordinance that fails to meet state law is null and void — and state standards apply instead. Ordinance 1890 is the city's compliance response.

The practical rule for a homeowner: if a local standard blocks your project, ask whether it is stricter than state law allows. Where the two conflict, state law wins (VMC section 16.303.15).

How many ADUs can I build on a Vallejo lot?

  • Single-family lot: three units in total — one JADU, one attached or conversion ADU, and one detached ADU.
  • Lot with an existing multifamily building: up to 8 detached ADUs, capped at the number of existing units; conversion ADUs inside existing non-livable space are allowed at a minimum of one and up to 25% of the existing units.
  • Lot with a proposed multifamily building: up to 2 detached ADUs.
  • ADUs and JADUs do not count toward the site's allowable residential density.

On top of these local limits, California requires every city to approve certain ADU types ministerially, including one ADU plus one JADU on a single-family lot and a detached new-construction ADU of up to 800 sq ft with 4 ft side and rear setbacks. Those by-right units cannot be refused for parking, or because the site has non-conforming conditions.

Vallejo ADU size, height and setback limits

ItemVallejo limit
Detached ADU maximum1,200 sq ft
Attached ADU maximumLesser of 50% of the main home's floor area or 1,200 sq ft
Conversion ADU (garage, interior)No minimum or maximum floor area
Minimum unit size190 sq ft from 8 October 2026 (150 sq ft before that)
JADU500 sq ft maximum, and it must sit within the walls of the house
Detached ADU height16 ft; 18 ft near major transit or on a multifamily multistory lot, plus 2 ft for an aligned roof pitch
Attached ADU heightUp to 25 ft, or the main home's limit if lower

Parking: Vallejo does require a space, with a long list of exceptions

Most summaries of Vallejo's rules state that no parking is required. That is wrong. The city requires one off-street space per ADU, and tandem spaces count. A space cannot be required, however, in any of these cases:

  • the ADU is 500 sq ft or less;
  • it sits within 1/2 mile walking distance of public transit;
  • it is in a historic district;
  • it is located entirely within the main dwelling or an accessory structure;
  • the street is permit-parking only and the city does not offer a permit to the ADU occupant;
  • a car-share vehicle is available within one block.

Two further points save money. No replacement parking is required when you demolish or convert a garage or carport for the ADU, and the by-right units listed in Government Code section 66323 cannot be conditioned on parking at all.

Owner occupancy, renting and selling a Vallejo ADU

  • An ADU does not require owner occupancy. State law bars the requirement for ADUs.
  • A JADU does under the current chapter; from 8 October 2026 the requirement applies only when the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the main home.
  • Rentals must be 30 days or longer. Short-term and vacation rentals of an ADU are not allowed in Vallejo.
  • The unit cannot be sold separately from the main house, and the deed restriction that records these limits is filed with the Solano County Assessor/Recorder — that is the county's only role inside the city, since Solano County's own zoning chapter governs unincorporated land only.

Permits, fees and the 60-day rule

  • Ministerial approval, no hearing. The city must approve or deny a complete application within 60 days; if it does nothing, the permit is deemed approved.
  • The 800 sq ft by-right ADU. Vallejo must allow at least an 800 sq ft ADU with 4 ft side and rear setbacks, and site rules such as lot coverage, floor-area ratio, open space and front setbacks cannot be used to preclude it.
  • Impact fees only above 750 sq ft, and only in proportion to what the main home would pay. Conversions and JADUs are not charged new utility connection or capacity fees.
  • Design standards apply narrowly: objective design rules for newly built attached or detached ADUs over 800 sq ft must be met; they do not apply to by-right state units.
  • Fire sprinklers and passageways cannot be imposed beyond what the main residence already requires.
  • Unpermitted ADUs: a unit built before 1 January 2020 can be legalised, and enforcement is delayed to 1 January 2030 where there is no health or safety issue.

Because the ordinance changed in October 2026, confirm the fee schedule and front setback for your specific zoning district with Vallejo Planning before you draw anything. The figures above come from the ordinance text, the city's own ADU summary sheet and California statute — all linked below.

faqs.q: How many ADUs can I build in Vallejo?
faqs.a: On a single-family lot, three units in total: one JADU plus one attached or conversion ADU plus one detached ADU. A lot with an existing multifamily building can take up to 8 detached ADUs, capped at the number of existing units, and interior conversion ADUs can be at least one and up to 25% of the existing units.

faqs.q: Do I have to live in the property to rent out a Vallejo ADU?
faqs.a: No for an ADU — California law bars an owner-occupancy requirement for ADUs and Vallejo dropped it. A JADU does require owner occupancy today, and from 8 October 2026 it does so only where the JADU shares sanitation facilities with the main home. Rentals must be for 30 consecutive days or longer.

faqs.q: Can I convert my garage into an ADU in Vallejo?
faqs.a: Yes. A legally built garage, barn or studio can be converted, and Vallejo treats a converted garage as a conversion ADU: no setback requirement, no minimum or maximum floor area, and no replacement parking. Demolishing a detached garage can be permitted at the same time as the ADU.

faqs.q: How long does a Vallejo ADU permit take?
faqs.a: Vallejo must approve or deny a complete ADU application within 60 days, and the review is ministerial with no public hearing. If the city misses the deadline, the permit is deemed approved under state law.

faqs.q: Do Vallejo's rules or California's rules apply?
faqs.a: Both, and state law wins where they conflict. California's ADU statutes (Government Code sections 66310 to 66342) set the floor: they limit what a city can require on size, setbacks, parking, owner occupancy and fees. Vallejo's chapter 16.303 adds local standards, but section 66316 makes a non-compliant ordinance null and void — which is why the state sent Vallejo a technical assistance letter in October 2025.

seo_title: Bellevue ADU Rules 2026: Size, Setbacks, Parking & DADU Permits
seo_desc: Bellevue ADU and DADU requirements checked against the city's Land Use Code: 1,200 sq ft maximum, 24 ft height, 10/15/5 ft setbacks, parking, owner occupancy and the building permit you actually need.
long_content:
Bellevue ADU rules changed twice in three years

Two ordinances explain why so much Bellevue ADU information online is out of date:

  • Ordinance 6746 (2023) — the ADU reform package. Bellevue repealed the owner-occupancy requirement, removed ADU design controls, dropped the registration and noticing process, and lifted the ban on selling an ADU separately from the main house.
  • Ordinance 6851 (adopted 24 June 2025, effective 1 July 2025) — Middle Housing. This is the change that matters most: before it, detached ADUs were not allowed in Bellevue at all. The middle housing amendments legalised them and allow up to two ADUs per lot, implementing Washington's HB 1110 and HB 1337.

Practical consequence: if an article tells you Bellevue requires the owner to live on site, caps an ADU at 1,000 sq ft, or that you cannot build a detached unit, it was written before mid-2025 and is describing rules that no longer exist.

What you can build in Bellevue: the 2026 limits

ItemBellevue limit
Maximum ADU floor area1,200 sq ft (up to 300 sq ft of parking or unheated storage excluded)
Detached ADU height24 ft — 28 ft when added over an existing accessory structure
Attached ADU heightThe same limit that applies to the main house
Setbacks, new detached ADU10 ft front / 15 ft rear / 5 ft side (SR-1 and SR-2, LUC 20.20.538)
Setbacks, attached ADUSame as the main house
Converted existing structureAllowed regardless of current setback or lot coverage compliance
Units per lotUp to 2 ADUs
Units counted for permit typeADUs count as regular dwelling units
Parking0 spaces under 1,000 sq ft or within 1/2 mile of a major transit stop; otherwise 1
Owner occupancyNot required
Impact feesCapped at 50% of the principal unit's fees

Two narrow limits are worth knowing early: a site cannot contain both an ADU and a home-occupation business, and no new ADU can be built on a unit lot created through a unit-lot or short subdivision.

Can I add an ADU to my existing Bellevue house?

Yes, and this is the cheapest route. An attached ADU (basement, converted garage, upper-floor addition) follows the main house's height and setback limits, and its floor area is not counted against the site's single-family floor-area allowance — so a big addition does not eat your FAR.

Conversions are the hidden advantage in Bellevue: the code lets you convert an existing structure into an ADU regardless of whether that structure currently meets the applicable setback and lot coverage dimensional requirements, and doing so does not make the property legally non-conforming. In most cities, a garage that sits too close to the property line is the reason a conversion fails. In Bellevue it is not a blocker.

Can I build a DADU (detached ADU) in Bellevue?

Since 1 July 2025, yes. Detached units are limited to 24 ft in height, or 28 ft when proposed as an addition over an existing accessory structure, and they follow the middle-housing dimensional table in LUC 20.20.538 (10 ft front, 15 ft rear, 5 ft side in the single-family zones). A detached ADU may be sited on the lot line that abuts an alley, which is how narrow lots usually make the numbers work.

Watch for one confusion that catches even experienced designers: the old detached accessory structure rules (LUC 20.20.125 — 5 ft rear setback, 15 ft height, 10% lot coverage) do not apply to detached ADUs. Mixing the two produces the wrong setback and the wrong height limit, which is exactly the mistake this page used to contain.

Parking, owner occupancy and design review: three rules people get wrong

  • Parking is not simply waived. Bellevue requires no off-street space for an ADU under 1,000 sq ft, or for one within 1/2 mile of a major transit stop. Outside those cases, one space per ADU is required. State law also caps what a city may ask: no parking within a 1/2-mile walk of a major transit stop, at most 1 space on lots under 6,000 sq ft, at most 2 on larger lots.
  • Owner occupancy is gone. The city repealed it in 2023 and RCW 36.70A.681 independently forbids cities from requiring the owner to live in the ADU or the main house.
  • Design review is gone. An ADU cannot face design or aesthetic requirements stricter than those applied to a single-family house, and Bellevue removed its extra design controls in 2023.

Which Bellevue building permit you need, and how the process runs

  • 1 or 2 units on the lot: a standard one- and two-family residence building permit.
  • 3 to 6 units in a single structure: the Middle Housing permit process.
  • More than 6 units: the commercial multifamily process.
  • ADUs count as dwelling units for this test, so adding a second ADU can push a project into the middle housing path.
  • One building permit is issued per building; a multi-building project may also need a separate clearing and grading site permit.
  • There is no ADU registry and no noticing requirement — that step was removed in 2023.

Start with a pre-application conversation with Bellevue's Development Services before you pay for drawings. Ask two questions that change projects: whether the lot carries a home-occupation business, and whether it was created by a unit-lot or short subdivision — either one can rule out a new ADU.

One amendment to watch

Ordinance 6931, passed on 28 July 2026, amends the units-per-lot provisions in LUC 20.20.120(C)(1) and 20.20.538(C)(1). It was pending codification at the time this page was written. If your project depends on the exact number of units you can build, confirm the current count with the city rather than relying on any guide, including this one.

faqs.q: Can I build a DADU in Bellevue?
faqs.a: Yes, but only since 1 July 2025. Detached ADUs were not allowed in Bellevue before Ordinance 6851 (the Middle Housing amendments) took effect. Detached units are limited to 24 ft in height, or 28 ft when built as an addition over an existing accessory structure, and they follow the dimensional table in LUC 20.20.538.

faqs.q: How many ADUs can I build in Bellevue?
faqs.a: Up to two ADUs on a lot where a single-family dwelling is allowed: two attached, one attached plus one detached, or two detached. Note that Ordinance 6931, passed on 28 July 2026, amends the units-per-lot provisions and was still pending codification when this page was written, so confirm the current count with Bellevue before you commit.

faqs.q: Do I have to live in my Bellevue house to rent out the ADU?
faqs.a: No. Bellevue removed its owner-occupancy requirement in 2023 and Washington law bars cities from requiring the owner to live in the ADU or the main house. Rentals of 30 consecutive days or more are allowed; short-term rentals may still be restricted by the city.

faqs.q: Do I need design review for an ADU in Bellevue?
faqs.a: No. Bellevue removed ADU design controls in 2023, and state law bars aesthetic requirements or design review for ADUs that are stricter than those applied to the principal unit.

faqs.q: What does a Bellevue ADU cost in impact fees?
faqs.a: Impact fees for an ADU are capped at 50% of what the same unit would be charged as a principal dwelling under RCW 36.70A.681. That cap is one of the biggest cost differences between Bellevue and California cities, where impact fees often apply in full above a size threshold.
